subject: C22
required_fixes: C22-F1 (high): Enforce actual token expiry at approval admission/decision. In crates/desktop-core/src/authority/harness_mcp.rs:177 and :842, expired() reads a failure flag; mcp_server_usable never compares now() with McpAuth.expires. Renewal sets that expiry but only a later renewal failure sets the flag. An approval held across expires_in, including sleep/wake, can therefore pass authority/harness_tools.rs:224 and send accept after the token expired. This violates DESIGN.md's independent native denial even when a server permits anonymous tools. The lapse test at tests/workspace_mcp/main.rs:544 calls expire_mcp_grants_for_tests(), masking the wall-clock case. Acceptance: hold an actual pending approval past its token deadline without another Send or manual expiry flag; Allow must produce decline, no tools/call, and keep inference usable. Also cover a call first offered after expiry.

C22-F2 (high): Block remote use while the catalog is loading or unavailable, without treating cached display data as current authority. authority/harness_mcp.rs:509 ignores CatalogState.loading/failure, list_mcp_servers retains the old catalog, and mcp_scope_current at :822 accepts an absent catalog with is_none_or. Consequently a failed same-workspace refresh leaves new starts, Send, history continuation and MCP approval authorized against stale revisions. DESIGN.md:1956 explicitly requires missing/loading/unavailable catalogs to block remote resume/Send until checked. The test without_its_catalog_a_scope_cannot_start_or_continue asserts the retained failure view but only tests Busy after switching workspaces; it never tests that failed cached catalog. Acceptance: start with a signed-in enabled server, hold/fail its catalog refresh, and prove remote admission/approval is blocked with draft/history preserved; only a successful fresh matching read permits continuation, while changed revision/removal retires the scope.

C22-F3 (high): Make server sign-out invalidate an in-progress sign-in for that same binding. authority/harness_mcp.rs:668 removes the stored grant but never cancels/invalidates mcp_flow; sign_in at :997 and :1014 subsequently commits based on that still-current flow and catalog. McpPanel exposes Sign out while Sign in again is waiting/completing, so a callback or delayed token response can silently sign the server back in after explicit sign-out. Acceptance: pause replacement sign-in both before callback and during token exchange, sign out, then release it; no replacement grant or usable token may be installed, the old conversation stays retired, and late issued tokens are revoked/cleaned up.

C22-F4 (high): Keep Keychain write ownership reserved through settlement. authority/harness_mcp.rs:387 removes writes_in_flight under one State lock before rotate (:414) or sign_in (:1011) acquires a separate lock to commit ownership. In that interval the new record is still pending_cleanup and unreserved; authority.rs:4702 can select it for deletion. Settlement can then save a grant pointing at a deleted record, with apparent success until relaunch. Acceptance: deterministically interleave cleanup between completed put and grant settlement for both initial sign-in and refresh; committed records must survive cleanup/relaunch, and failed/stale records must remain tracked and be deleted. Releasing the reservation and settling ownership must be atomic with respect to cleanup selection.

C22-F5 (high): Do not approve an MCP call whose consequential arguments the operator cannot inspect. harness/session.rs:1459 cuts the serialized actual arguments to MAX_COMMAND_TEXT (2048 bytes plus ellipsis) before storing McpItem; on_elicitation copies only that prefix into the approval. decisions-panel.tsx:98 offers Approve once without the omitted arguments, while the engine executes the full original call. Two requests with the same long padding prefix but different later targets/actions present the same approval. This newly extends C21's incomplete approval-display problem to remote MCP calls. Acceptance: provide the complete bounded, redacted call arguments through an inspectable approval, or refuse oversized calls; a material field beyond byte 2048 must never execute on approval of a prefix alone.
evidence_gaps: C22-G1: Mandatory T23 coverage is absent for this MCP slice. The eight workspace_mcp tests and C22 native N01-N07 do not disconnect during a pending approval or an admitted tools/call, reconnect, and establish no automatic replay plus an honest uncertain remote outcome. Add source-bound offline/reconnect evidence, explicit retry behavior and offline access to protected MCP-scoped history. Catalog failure and a pre-start refused refresh are not substitutes for an interrupted remote call.

C22-G2: The required combined Gateway/MCP rotation branch is not exercised. workspace_mcp uses a stored workspace API key and tests MCP-only rotation; harness_identity_history tests Gateway renewal without an MCP scope. Provide one production-interface scenario with both credentials due and WorkspaceWrite enabled: one fresh confirmation, decline preserving the draft without Send, then acceptance producing one combined restart/compatible restore and exactly one explicit turn, with no stale approvals or tool-call replay.

C22-G3: The requested trace-correlation fixtures are missing. workspace_mcp/fixture.rs returns a constant RESULT and the native MCP fixture returns C22-NATIVE-MCP-RESULT; tests/driver assert result text and bearer/call counts, not correlation to a distinct call trace. Supply synthetic protocol-faithful trace/execution evidence linking the actual approved call, server response and displayed/recorded outcome, including denial and an unrelated trace. Live Gateway trace behavior remains correctly reserved for C25.
optional_suggestions: Strengthen native C22-N06: the driver programmatically focuses Approve once and then records Tab reaching Decline and Message; evaluate() only requires Decline. Record reaching and activating Approve once through keyboard navigation as well, matching the checklist's stated coverage.
